JOHNSON AND SONS CLINIC - DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient: John Cobb DOB: 03/02/1962 Sex: M MRN: 854030

Admit: 07/12/2015 Discharge: 07/20/2015

Admitting Diagnosis: Barrett's esophagus with dysplasia (other type)
Secondary Diagnosis: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) with fibrosis stage F2

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
John Cobb, a 63-year-old male, presented to Johnson and Sons Clinic with a history of Barrett's esophagus diagnosed on July 12, 2015, and non-alcoholic fatty disease (NAFLD) with fibrosis stage F2 diagnosed on October 29, 2011. He was admitted for further evaluation and management of his conditions.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
1. Barrett's esophagus with other type dysplasia, diagnosed on July 12, 2015.
2. Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) with fibrosis stage F2, diagnosed on October 29, 2011.
3. Former smoker - 1 pack per day, quit on February 10, 2018.
4. Consumes approximately 24 alcoholic drinks per week.
5. Family history significant for type 2 diabetes in his father, who was diagnosed at age G9 and passed away at age 87.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
Mr. Cobb's hospital course was uneventful. He underwent routine blood tests, liver function tests, and imaging studies to assess the severity of his NAFLD and Barrett's esophagus. The results were consistent with his known diagnoses, and no acute complications were noted.

During his hospital stay, Mr. Cobb's blood pressure was recorded at 142/81 mmHg on February 8, 2026, and 131/79 mmHg on January 12, 2025. His weight was 188 pounds on February 8, 2026, 185 pounds on January 12, 2025, and 194 pounds on December 17, 2023. His physical was unremarkable, with no signs of acute distress or complications related to his gastrointestinal conditions.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Mr. Cobb was discharged home without any new medications. He was advised to continue his current regimen and follow-up with his gastroenterologist for ongoing management of Barrett's esophagus and NAFLD.

DISCHARGE PLAN:
Mr. Cobb was discharged home in stable condition on July 20, 2015. He was instructed to maintain a healthy lifestyle, including a balanced diet and regular exercise, to help manage his NAFLD. He was also advised to abstain from smoking and limit his alcohol consumption.

FOLLOW-UP:
Mr. Cobb is scheduled to follow up with Dr. Aaron Howard, his gastroenterologist at Johnson and Sons Clinic, in one month for a routine check-up and further management of his Barrett's esophagus and NAFLD. He will also continue to follow up with his primary care physician for general health maintenance.

OUNSELING:
Mr. Cobb was counseled on the of maintaining a healthy lifestyle, including a balanced diet, regular exercise, and limiting alcohol consumption, to help manage his NAFLD. He was also reminded of the importance of attending all scheduled follow-up appointments with his healthcare providers.
